commits.message:
Hold the forced readiness probe's request at one instant

The raw-probe readiness cases force the probe by setting the provider
evidence bound to 1 ms, and the handler then reads the probe's own
success back under that same bound. A runner that stalls for 2 ms or
more between the probe's completion and the handler's read sees the
fresh success as stale, so the healthy case reports
providerQueryHealthy false (node shard 1/3 on CI). Injecting a 3 ms
stall at that point fails both healthy cases every run.

The fixture now freezes Date for a forced-probe request, so the probe's
completion and the handler's read share one clock reading. Production is
unchanged: its bound defaults to 30 s and nothing between the two reads
waits on I/O.

Count the event loop's turns during a foreign block's import

The import test bounded the longest stretch without a timer tick by five
transactions' share of the run's wall-clock total. The stretch before the
first transaction (decoding the block, and the process's first evaluation)
is a quarter to a third of a 16-transaction run, so a loaded runner crossed
the bound with the yields in place. An immediate that re-queues itself
runs once per turn: the import gives one turn per transaction (16), and
none without the per-event yield.

Read the confirmed proof's own reservation by id in the collateral release test

The store lists reservations by id. The test took the first record as the
proof's own, which held only while the proof's derived reservation id
sorted before the peer's fixed one. Wiring the unused-script-witness family
into the catalogue (e25aff33a) changed the deployment roster, and with it
the derived id, so the test read the peer's record instead. Production
behaves as intended: the proof selects fresh collateral, and the store
refuses to re-lease collateral the peer holds.

Size the duplicate-asset maximum shape at the 5,000-byte value cap

Since the ledger-output scan refuses a Value over 5,000 bytes (b8c10beee),
an accepted output filled with assets to the 16,384-byte output bound is no
longer canonical, so its twin cannot be. The real maximum for a repeat at
the last asset name is the value at the cap in both the accepted and the
forced case; the shape test now also shows one more byte is past it.

Re-measure the largest validation-dispute wallet move after the value cap

The ledger-output scan's 5,000-byte Value check (b8c10beee) adds 22 bytes
to each ledger-output descriptor summary yield. The script-sources output
proof finalize hop attaches the datum and value summary yields, so its
reference scripts now total 34,693 bytes (14,748 + 12,405 + 7,540).

Read and write long Flat naturals in linear time

Since builtins are evaluated through the pinned evaluator (d69f634ff),
every builtin value crosses as a Flat constant. The Flat reader and
writer shifted a bigint once per 7-bit group, which is quadratic in the
value's length: decoding the integer byteStringToInteger gives for a
49,784-byte input took about 200 ms and allocated gigabytes, and a
proof-mode run evaluates that application three times. Long naturals now
go through their bytes; short ones keep the shifting path.

The staged-conversion test also dropped its second check of the last
conversion and the per-order test that repeated the 49,784 and 49,785
byte rows' assertions; every boundary row still runs.

Pin the forced output Value cap from mint to block and drop a reason with no producer

A forced transaction with a 5,001-byte output Value is refused at the order
mint; built directly, it classifies as an output canonicity rejection, the
replay and the DA payload agree, and block production continues. The honest
rejection cannot be convicted and the acceptance is. The admission-stopped
readiness reason has had no producer since the forced screens were removed.
